figurative_meaning_en: Temporary detachment or renunciation, often a fleeting realization of the futility of worldly life upon witnessing death at a cremation ground
similar_in_english: Memento mori (reminder of death leading to reflection)
Deathbed conversion (sudden change in outlook near death)
example_sentences_in_bangla: শ্মশানে গিয়ে তার শ্মশান বৈরাগ্য জাগল, কিন্তু বাড়ি ফিরে সব ভুলে গেল।
এই শ্মশান বৈরাগ্য স্থায়ী হয় না, শুধু ক্ষণিকের জন্য।
example_sentences_in_english: Upon visiting the cremation ground, he experienced shmashan boiraggo, but forgot it all once back home.
This shmashan boiraggo is not permanent; it's only momentary.
history: This idiom draws from Hindu and Buddhist philosophical traditions where exposure to death at cremation grounds (shmashan) prompts a brief sense of vairagya or detachment from material world, emphasizing life's impermanence.
note: Rooted in Vaishnava and Shaiva literature, often used to critique insincere spiritual awakenings.
